fields.meta_title: Bankruptcy Intake Form With Creditor Lists | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a bankruptcy intake form that collects creditors, income, property, and expenses, and flags urgent sale dates for an attorney. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Bankruptcy Intake Form That Lists Every Debt
fields.hero_description: Build a bankruptcy intake form that lists each creditor with its balance and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Attorney Has Before the Consultation
fields.features_subheading: Every answer lands in a field of its own, and the attorney reads debts and income as one record.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the house and the car

Answer yes to owning a home and the form asks who holds the mortgage and whether a sale date is set. Answer no and it moves on to vehicles, with no blank lender fields left behind.
fields.feature_2:
One row per creditor, with a running total

Prospects add each debt as its own row with the creditor, the type of debt, and the balance. The form adds up the balances as they go and shows the total at the top of the list.
fields.feature_3:
Pay stubs read into the income section

Upload a pay stub and the app reads its date and gross amount into the income section. A value it reads with low confidence goes to a paralegal, who checks it against the stub.
fields.feature_4:
Last year's tax return, attached on upload

Ask for the most recent tax return as an upload on the same form. The file is saved with the prospect's answers, and nobody has to request it again after the consultation is booked.
fields.feature_5:
Monthly expenses in plain categories

Ask for rent or mortgage, utilities, food, transportation, and child care as separate monthly amounts. Each amount is saved as its own number, ready for the attorney's first review.
fields.feature_6:
The whole codebase in your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when the intake has to sit next to the firm's case software. Keep building on it there, or keep prompting changes.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Each Intake Goes After Submit
fields.tab_content_1:
$38,940 in debts, each creditor on its own row

Beatrix Molyneux fills in Eastbrook Bankruptcy Law's intake the night before her consultation. She adds 4 creditors, each with its type and balance, including a $6,215 hospital bill. The app totals them at $38,940. Paralegal Henrike Dablow gets an email with the full table and reads it before the meeting.
fields.tab_content_2:
With 9 days to the sale, the attorney calls that afternoon

Teodoro Nwachukwu tells Marrowby Law that Ashcombe Home Loans has set a foreclosure sale for his house. He enters the sale date, 9 days away. Any sale date within 14 days sends attorney Ysanne Corrigal an email with his phone number. She calls him that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_3:
Pay stubs read into income, all but the blurry one

Annika Varkey uploads 6 pay stubs to Brindlewood Legal's intake from her phone. The app pulls the pay date and gross pay off each stub for her income section. One photo is too blurry to read with confidence. Its gross pay goes to paralegal Fenna Stoddart, who asks Annika for a clearer photo.
fields.tab_content_4:
One certificate past 180 days, with a flag for review

Lucius Ambergate tells Kingsbury Legal Aid Clinic that he finished credit counseling, and he uploads the certificate. The app reads the counseling date and finds it 212 days old. Any certificate older than 180 days is flagged for staff attorney Rosamund Thorncliffe, who sees it before his appointment.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Bankruptcy Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a bankruptcy intake form that gathers debts, income, property, and expenses before the first consultation.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put deadlines on the first screen
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Give every debt a row of its own
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for files beside the questions
fields.howto_step_1_des: A consumer practice asks about credit cards and medical bills. A firm that also files for sole proprietors adds business debts and equipment. Write both lists before you describe anything, because each one becomes its own branch of questions.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about foreclosure sales and wage garnishments before anything else. Choose how many days out should alert an attorney, and name the person who gets that email. Add a backup attorney for evenings and weekends.
fields.howto_step_3_des: On each row, ask who is owed and how much, plus the last four digits of the account. Keep adding rows until the prospect says they are done. A stack of collection letters is easier to enter one at a time.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Place the pay stub upload inside the income section and the tax return upload beside the tax questions. Ask for the counseling certificate where you ask about counseling. Prospects then upload each file while the question is in front of them.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the branches and the deadline alert into one prompt, uploads included. Emergent builds the bankruptcy intake form, the database behind it, and a review screen for staff. Change any question later by asking for it in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send finished intakes to the paralegal who prepares the first review, and urgent ones to an attorney. Each person gets an email with the intake attached. Name a second reader for weeks the paralegal is out.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in one intake as a renter with credit card debt and one as a homeowner with a sale next week. Upload a blurry photo as a pay stub. Check that the totals add up and the attorney email arrives.

faq_plan.q: What is a bankruptcy intake form?
faq_plan.a: A bankruptcy intake form is the questionnaire a prospective client fills in before meeting a bankruptcy lawyer. It gathers personal, financial, property, employment, and debt information, so the lawyer has the client's whole picture in one place. The firm then starts the petition from those answers.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a bankruptcy intake form?
faq_plan.a: Write down the sections your firm needs and who reads each finished intake. Put both in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it from that description. When a question needs to change, ask for the change the same way.

faq_plan.q: What should a bankruptcy intake form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Start with what the official bankruptcy forms need: a list of all creditors with the amount and nature of each claim, and the source, amount, and frequency of income. Then add a list of the client's property and a detailed list of monthly living expenses. Contact details and household size round it out.

faq_plan.q: Can a bankruptcy intake form also take injury cases?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the first question decides which section opens. A personal injury intake form asks about the accident and the insurers. The bankruptcy section asks about debts instead. Ask the type of matter first and show only the matching section. Both kinds of intake can still land in one database.

faq_plan.q: Should a bankruptcy intake form ask about credit counseling?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Under the Bankruptcy Code, an individual must have received credit counseling from an approved agency within 180 days before filing, with exceptions in emergency situations. Ask whether the prospect has finished it and for the date on the certificate. The attorney then decides what happens next.

faq_plan.q: Which documents should a bankruptcy intake form collect?
faq_plan.a: Ask for recent pay stubs and the latest tax return. Debtors must give the case trustee a copy of the tax return or transcripts for the most recent tax year, and collecting it at intake saves asking for it later. Add the counseling certificate if the prospect has one.

faq_plan.q: Should a bankruptcy intake form screen out other kinds of cases?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with one question at the start. Ask what the person needs help with, and send divorce or landlord matters to a general legal intake form instead of the debt questions. Emergent builds that first question and both forms from one plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can clients fill out a bankruptcy intake form on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A form that shows one question per screen fits a phone, which helps when someone enters debts one letter at a time from a pile of mail. Pay stubs and collection letters upload straight from the camera. Emergent builds that conversational flow with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Where do bankruptcy intake forms store client answers?
faq_plan.a: When the form is built with Emergent, each intake lands in a database the firm owns. Staff open each one from the review screen. On paid plans, the firm can also export the full code to its own GitHub repository.

faq_plan.q: How should a bankruptcy intake form list medical bills?
faq_plan.a: List each provider's bill as a creditor of its own, with the balance and the account number from the statement. Unlike a patient intake form, it asks nothing about symptoms or treatment. A hospital stay and the lab work from that stay become two rows when they are billed separately.

plan.angle: The results for this query are law firm and court clinic questionnaires and template galleries: long pages of blank lines for debts, income and property. This page shows the intake a bankruptcy practice runs once answers arrive: each creditor in its own row with a total, a foreclosure sale date close enough to email an attorney, pay stubs read into the income section with an unclear one sent to a paralegal, and a credit counseling certificate older than 180 days flagged before the appointment. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what the official forms need, mixed practices, counseling, documents, screening other matters, phones, where answers live and medical bills. No legal or financial advice: the page describes what a firm collects and routes, never whether someone should file.
